\vfill{}

The spidergram package provides a comprehensive LaTeX solution for generating visually rich spidergrams—a specialized network diagram used to map complex agricultural or management systems (e.g., farming operations, livestock pathways). By integrating the specific structural demands of the spidergram method into a convenient TeX environment and as a dedicated TikZ library, this package significantly simplifies and standardizes the visualization process for researchers in agriculture/equine enterprises and sustainable resource management.

The underlying methodology for representing farms via the spidergram was originally published by Aeres Hogeschool \cite{methorst_het_2026}. The website is \href{https://en.boerenboom.nl/}{Boerenboom}. This LaTeX tool ensures that complex data sets can be reproduced accurately and professionally within academic publications. 

For questions regarding the package email Carsten Schulz: \href{mailto:koryphaeen@posteo.net}{koryphaeen@posteo.net}

\section{Prerequisites/Setup}
To begin using the spidergram package, users must load both the necessary TikZ package and the custom library. The following commands should be placed within the document's preamble:
\medskip{}
\texttt{\textbackslash usepackage\{tikz\}}
\texttt{\textbackslash usepackage{\{spidergram\}}
\texttt{\textbackslash usetikzlibrary\{spidergram\}}

\section{How to use}

\subsection{Specifications in the preamble}

\texttt{\textbackslash usepackage{[}english{]}\{spidergram\}}

\texttt{\%included languages options: romanian, dutch, croatian, german,
english, latin, finnish, svedish}

\texttt{\%included predefined colors }

\texttt{\textbackslash sgcolor\{tealblue\} \%(standard and original
color)}

\texttt{\%for generation flexibility redefine via one of these}

\texttt{\%\textbackslash sgcolor\{bole\}}

\texttt{\%\textbackslash sgcolor\{byzantinum\}}

\texttt{\%\textbackslash sgcolor\{sapgreen\}}

\texttt{\%\textbackslash sgcolor\{vividburgundy\}}

\texttt{\%\textbackslash sgcolor\{yaleblue\}}

\texttt{\%the color of the lines in the diagram is defined as:}

\texttt{\%\textbackslash dgcolor\{darkgray\}}

\newpage{}

\subsection{Examples}

Practical Application Examples The following examples demonstrate the usage of \boeren and \paarden with real-world data \cite{baumann_practical_nodate}. These functions accept a sequence of numerical values, representing connectivity or size metrics at each node in the diagram.

\subsubsection{Example, Boerenboom\protect\marginpar{Farming Tree}}

\medskip{}

\texttt{\textbackslash begin\{tikzpicture\}{[}scale=0.6, every node/.style=\{scale=0.4\}{]}}

\texttt{\textbackslash boeren\{4,4,8,7.5,7,6,5,5,4,9,7,7,6,9,7,8,5,8\}}

\texttt{\textbackslash end\{tikzpicture\}}

\medskip{}
\texttt{\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.6, every node/.style={scale=0.4}]
\boeren{4,4,8,7.5,7,6,5,5,4,9,7,7,6,9,7,8,5,8}
\end{tikzpicture}}

\newpage{}

\subsubsection{Example, Paardenboom\protect\marginpar{Equine Tree}}

\medskip{}

\texttt{\textbackslash begin\{tikzpicture\}{[}scale=0.6, every node/.style=\{scale=0.4\}{]}}

\texttt{\textbackslash paarden\{8,9,10,3.5,10,7,6,7,5,7,9,8,9,4,7,9.5,5,8\}}

\texttt{\textbackslash end\{tikzpicture\}}

\medskip{}

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.6, every node/.style={scale=0.4}]
\paarden{8,9,10,3.5,10,7,6,7,5,7,9,8,9,4,7,9.5,5,8}
\end{tikzpicture}
